heroHeadline: New Santa Cruz blockades and a YPFB intervention as VP Lara publicly breaks with Paz over Cerimedo
heroSubtitle: Producers installed fresh 24-hour blockades at four points in Santa Cruz department (San Julián, Yapacaní, Cuatro Cañadas, Los Troncos) on Sept. 2 over the diesel-price decree, prompting the government to place state oil company YPFB under 180-day intervention rather than repeal it, as the boliviano hit a new floated-era record of Bs. 12.26/$1. Separately, Vice President Edmand Lara publicly broke with President Paz on Sept. 1, citing forensic evidence of "sustained contact" between Fernando Cerimedo's phone and Nadia Beller's shooters and new photographs placing Cerimedo inside the presidential headquarters and Bolivia's official delegation to a March meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
